subproblem.title: C¹ local inverse with surjective inverse derivative (inverse function theorem on ℝ^d)
subproblem.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝ^d → ℝ^d (Euclid d), V ⊆ ℝ^d open and v₀ ∈ V. Assume Φ is C¹ on V and its derivative DΦ(v₀) is injective. Then there exist open sets V₁, O ⊆ ℝ^d and a map H : ℝ^d → ℝ^d such that v₀ ∈ V₁ ⊆ V, Φ(v₀) ∈ O, H is C¹ on O, H(O) = V₁, Φ(H(w)) = w for every w ∈ O, and the derivative DH(w) is surjective for every w ∈ O.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (Φ : Euclid d → Euclid d) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (v₀ : Euclid d), IsOpen V → v₀ ∈ V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 Φ V → Injective (fderiv ℝ Φ v₀) → ∃ (V₁ O : Set (Euclid d)) (H : Euclid d → Euclid d), IsOpen V₁ ∧ IsOpen O ∧ v₀ ∈ V₁ ∧ V₁ ⊆ V ∧ Φ v₀ ∈ O ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 H O ∧ H '' O = V₁ ∧ (∀ w ∈ O, Φ (H w) = w) ∧ ∀ w ∈ O, Surjective (fderiv ℝ H w)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof (selected node local_inverse), steps 2–6 (pointwise regularity, invertible derivative at v₀, persistence of invertibility, inverse function theorem restricted to the invertibility region, C¹ inverse with derivative E_v⁻¹), stated for a general map Φ that is C¹ on an open V ⊆ Euclid d instead of Φ = F ∘ ψ on V₀ ∩ ψ⁻¹(U). Conventions: E := Euclid d; "C¹" means ContDiff(On/At) ℝ 1; DΦ := fderiv ℝ Φ. No import beyond GMT.Ch07.Submission is needed or allowed (a leaf inserts only its theorem); every lemma cited below is available there.
1. (Pointwise regularity.) Since V is open and Φ is C¹ on V, Φ is C¹ at every v ∈ V (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt, using V ∈ 𝓝 v); hence Φ is differentiable at v (ContDiffAt.differentiableAt, 1 ≠ 0) and HasFDerivAt Φ (DΦ(v)) v.
2. (Invertible derivative at v₀.) DΦ(v₀) is an injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space E, hence bijective. So E₀ := (LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo DΦ(v₀) hinj).toContinuousLinearEquiv is a continuous linear equivalence E ≃L[ℝ] E whose coercion to E →L[ℝ] E equals DΦ(v₀) (the two maps agree at every vector by definition). By step 1, HasFDerivAt Φ E₀ v₀.
3. (Invertibility persists.) The map v ↦ DΦ(v) is continuous on the open set V (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen, 1 ≤ 1). The set R of continuous linear maps E →L[ℝ] E that are coercions of continuous linear equivalences E ≃L[ℝ] E is open (ContinuousLinearEquiv.isOpen; E is complete). Hence V₁′ := V ∩ DΦ⁻¹(R) is open (ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage), and v₀ ∈ V₁′ because DΦ(v₀) = E₀ by step 2. For every v ∈ V₁′ choose E_v : E ≃L[ℝ] E with E_v = DΦ(v); then HasFDerivAt Φ E_v v by step 1 (v ∈ V).
4. (Inverse function theorem, restricted to V₁′.) By step 1, Φ is C¹ at v₀, so HasStrictFDerivAt Φ DΦ(v₀) v₀ (ContDiffAt.hasStrictFDerivAt, 1 ≠ 0), i.e. HasStrictFDerivAt Φ E₀ v₀ by step 2. HasStrictFDerivAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph yields an open partial homeomorphism Φ̃ : E → E whose coercion is Φ (HasStrictFDerivAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_coe) and with v₀ ∈ Φ̃.source (HasStrictFDerivAt.mem_toOpenPartialHomeomorph_source). Let Φ₁ := Φ̃.restrOpen V₁′ (V₁′ is open by step 3). Its coercion is still Φ, and Φ₁.source = Φ̃.source ∩ V₁′ (OpenPartialHomeomorph.restrOpen_source). Put V₁ := Φ₁.source, O := Φ₁.target and H := Φ₁.symm. Then V₁ and O are open (open_source, open_target); v₀ ∈ V₁ (as v₀ ∈ Φ̃.source and v₀ ∈ V₁′); V₁ ⊆ V₁′ ⊆ V; Φ(v₀) = Φ₁(v₀) ∈ O (map_source); H '' O = V₁ (symm_image_target_eq_source); and Φ(H w) = Φ₁(Φ₁.symm w) = w for every w ∈ O (right_inv).
5. (H is C¹ with surjective derivative.) Let w ∈ O and v := H w. Then v ∈ Φ₁.source = V₁ ⊆ V₁′ (map_target), so by step 3 there is E_v : E ≃L[ℝ] E with E_v = DΦ(v) and HasFDerivAt Φ₁ E_v v (Φ₁ coerces to Φ), and Φ₁ is C¹ at v by step 1 (v ∈ V). OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm (applied with w ∈ Φ₁.target) shows that H = Φ₁.symm is C¹ at w; as w ∈ O was arbitrary, H is C¹ on O (ContDiffAt.contDiffWithinAt at each point). OpenPartialHomeomorph.hasFDerivAt_symm gives HasFDerivAt H E_v.symm w, hence fderiv ℝ H w = E_v.symm (HasFDerivAt.fderiv), which is surjective because E_v.symm is an equivalence.
6. (Conclusion.) V₁, O and H satisfy: V₁ and O are open, v₀ ∈ V₁ ⊆ V, Φ(v₀) ∈ O, H is C¹ on O, H '' O = V₁, and Φ(H w) = w and DH(w) is surjective for every w ∈ O. ∎
proof_key_steps: Pointwise: Φ is C¹ and differentiable at every v ∈ V (V open), with HasFDerivAt Φ (DΦ v) v.
DΦ(v₀) is an injective endomorphism of the finite-dimensional E, so it is the coercion of E₀ : E ≃L[ℝ] E (LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo, toContinuousLinearEquiv).
Invertibility persists on the open set V₁′ := V ∩ DΦ⁻¹(range of the coercion from E ≃L[ℝ] E), which contains v₀ (continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen, ContinuousLinearEquiv.isOpen, isOpen_inter_preimage).

HasStrictFDerivAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph (via ContDiffAt.hasStrictFDerivAt) restricted to V₁′ (restrOpen) gives V₁ := source ∋ v₀, O := target ∋ Φ v₀ and H := symm, with V₁ ⊆ V, H '' O = V₁ and Φ ∘ H = id on O.
At each w ∈ O, contDiffAt_symm makes H C¹ at w and hasFDerivAt_symm gives fderiv ℝ H w = E_v.symm with v = H w, which is surjective.

subproblem.title: Images of open subsets under a proper injective chart are relatively open
subproblem.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, M, W ⊆ ℝ^P, V, V₁ ⊆ ℝ^d and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P. Assume W is open, ψ is continuous on V and injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, V₁ is open and V₁ ⊆ V. Then there is an open set N₀ ⊆ ℝ^P with M ∩ N₀ = ψ(V₁).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (M W : Set (Euclid P)) (V V₁ : Set (Euclid d)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P), IsOpen W → ContinuousOn ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W ∩ M → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → IsOpen V₁ → V₁ ⊆ V → ∃ N₀ : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen N₀ ∧ M ∩ N₀ = ψ '' V₁
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof (selected node local_inverse), step 8 (ψ(V₁) is relatively open in M), stated for an arbitrary open V₁ ⊆ V and arbitrary dimensions P, d. Conventions: B_r(x) := ball x r; distances are Euclidean. No import beyond GMT.Ch07.Submission is needed. The accepted lemma Submission.dsmc_chart_inverse_continuity is supplied by the sibling reuse child chart_inverse_continuity, listed in depends_on so that it is merged into this leaf's Lean base.
1. (ψ(V) ⊆ W.) ψ(V) = W ∩ M ⊆ W.
2. (Local radii.) Let v ∈ V₁. As V₁ is open, choose ε_v > 0 with B_{ε_v}(v) ⊆ V₁ (Metric.isOpen_iff). Apply the accepted lemma Submission.dsmc_chart_inverse_continuity to P, d, V, W, ψ (ψ is continuous and injective on V, ψ(V) ⊆ W by step 1, and V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W), to the point v ∈ V (since V₁ ⊆ V) and to ε_v > 0: this gives δ_v > 0 such that every v′ ∈ V with dist(ψ v′, ψ v) < δ_v satisfies dist(v′, v) < ε_v, hence v′ ∈ B_{ε_v}(v) ⊆ V₁. Choose such δ_v for all v ∈ V₁ simultaneously (in Lean, `choose` on the statement ∀ v ∈ V₁, ∃ δ > 0, ∀ v′ ∈ V, dist (ψ v′) (ψ v) < δ → v′ ∈ V₁; then δ_v depends on the proof of v ∈ V₁).
3. (Definition of N₀.) Put N₀ := ⋃_{v ∈ V₁} (W ∩ B_{δ_v}(ψ v)). Each W ∩ B_{δ_v}(ψ v) is open (W is open and balls are open), so N₀ is open (isOpen_iUnion applied to the outer union over v and to the inner union over the proof of v ∈ V₁).
4. (M ∩ N₀ ⊆ ψ(V₁).) Let x ∈ M with x ∈ W ∩ B_{δ_v}(ψ v) for some v ∈ V₁. Then x ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), so x = ψ(v′) for some v′ ∈ V, and dist(ψ v′, ψ v) < δ_v. By step 2, v′ ∈ V₁, so x = ψ(v′) ∈ ψ(V₁).
5. (ψ(V₁) ⊆ M ∩ N₀.) Let v ∈ V₁. Then v ∈ V, so ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ M; thus ψ(v) ∈ M and ψ(v) ∈ W, and ψ(v) ∈ B_{δ_v}(ψ v) because δ_v > 0. Hence ψ(v) ∈ W ∩ B_{δ_v}(ψ v) ⊆ N₀, so ψ(v) ∈ M ∩ N₀.
6. (Conclusion.) N₀ is open and, by steps 4 and 5, M ∩ N₀ = ψ(V₁). ∎
proof_key_steps: ψ(V) ⊆ W because ψ(V) = W ∩ M.
For each v ∈ V₁, take ε_v with B_{ε_v}(v) ⊆ V₁ and δ_v > 0 from the accepted Submission.dsmc_chart_inverse_continuity, so v′ ∈ V and dist(ψ v′, ψ v) < δ_v imply v′ ∈ V₁.
N₀ := ⋃_{v ∈ V₁} (W ∩ B_{δ_v}(ψ v)) is open (isOpen_iUnion twice).
M ∩ N₀ ⊆ ψ(V₁): a point of M ∩ W ∩ B_{δ_v}(ψ v) is ψ(v′) with v′ ∈ V (W ∩ M = ψ(V)) and then v′ ∈ V₁.
ψ(V₁) ⊆ M ∩ N₀: for v ∈ V₁, ψ(v) ∈ W ∩ M and ψ(v) ∈ B_{δ_v}(ψ v).

Their union defines an open N₀, and the proof establishes both inclusions in M ∩ N₀ = ψ '' V₁. Every prerequisite is supplied, including when V₁ is empty.
